name: spawn
title: world.spawn
lead: Puts an entity at a point and returns its handle. A mob kind of the game by name (`world.spawn("cow", pos)`) is the game's own entity, and takes no `data`. A pack's own kind takes the data it starts life holding. `nil` for a kind nothing defined and this game does not have.
signature: world.spawn(def: EntityDef | string, pos: Vec3, data: { [string]: any }?) → EntityHandle ?

usedIn.quote: assigning the whole record again. This works on handles from `world.spawn` and
`mob = false`. Pass it to `world.spawn` just like the handle from `define`.
